webhooks.summary: GitHub exposes a large catalog of webhook events delivered via HTTP POST to a URL you control. Webhooks can be configured at the repository, organization, or GitHub App level. Each delivery includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header for payload verification.

managementEndpoints.description: Test the push event delivery of a repository webhook

signature.detail: GitHub computes `HMAC-SHA256(webhook_secret, raw_request_body)` and sends the hex digest in the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header prefixed with `sha256=`. To verify, recompute the HMAC using the same secret and the raw (unmodified) request body, then compare against the header value using a constant-time comparison. If no secret is configured when creating the webhook, the signature header will be absent. An older `X-Hub-Signature` header (SHA-1) may also be present but `X-Hub-Signature-256` is the recommended primary verification mechanism.

setupSteps.title: Obtain the inbound hook URL from your registry workspace
setupSteps.detail: Copy the stable inbound hook URL provided by your package registry workspace. This is the target GitHub will POST event payloads to.

setupSteps.title: Generate a webhook secret
setupSteps.detail: Generate a random, high-entropy secret string (e.g., 32+ bytes). This secret will be used by GitHub to sign each delivery and by your receiver to verify the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header. Store it securely.

setupSteps.title: Prepare your receiver endpoint
setupSteps.detail: Ensure your server is publicly reachable over HTTPS, accepts POST requests at the hook URL path, reads the raw request body (do not re-serialize or modify it), and responds with HTTP 200 to acknowledge receipt.

setupSteps.title: Implement signature verification
setupSteps.detail: On every incoming request, read the raw body bytes and the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw_body)` and compare the hex digest to the header value (after the `sha256=` prefix) using a constant-time comparison. Reject requests that do not match. Also inspect the `X-Github-Event` header to route the payload to the correct handler.

setupSteps.title: Create the webhook via the GitHub REST API
setupSteps.detail: POST to `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` for a repository webhook, or `https://api.github.com/orgs/{org}/hooks` for an organization webhook. The request body must include: `config.url` set to your inbound hook URL, `config.content_type` set to `json`, `config.secret` set to the secret from step 2, and `events` set to an array of event names you wish to subscribe to (e.g., `["push", "registry-package-published", "package-published"]`). Authenticate with a token that has admin access to the repository or organization. Reference: https://docs.github.com/rest/

setupSteps.title: Verify the ping event
setupSteps.detail: GitHub automatically sends a `ping` event (`X-Github-Event: ping`) immediately after webhook creation. Confirm your endpoint receives it, verifies the signature, and responds with HTTP 200.

setupSteps.title: Register the hook URL in the registry webhooks area
setupSteps.detail: Within your package registry workspace's webhooks settings area, confirm or register the same inbound hook URL so that registry-internal workflows triggered by GitHub events are properly wired. Ensure the configured events match the ones you selected when creating the GitHub webhook.
